\n
\n

\n Notes:\n \n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Exceptions to height regulations: The height limitations contained in the official\n height and area regulations do not apply to public utility structures, spires, belfries,\n cupolas, antennas, water tanks, ventilators, chimneys or other appurtenances usually\n required to be placed above the roof level and not intended for human occupancy except\n where the height of such structures will constitute a hazard to the safe landing and\n takeoff of aircraft at an established airport.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Zero Lot Line: Townhouse/Rowhouse developments shall be permitted to reduce the interior\n side yard setback to zero, provided the reduction does not create health or safety\n issues and can satisfy utility easements.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The minimum lot size of all parcels created through the lot split process shall be\n one (1) acre, with the exception of public utility lots.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n 4.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n There shall be no minimum lot size that applies to a public utility lot. Public Utility\n lots will not be subject to setbacks.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n For all residential districts:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n When a lot's side property boundaries are not parallel or the lot has an odd configuration\n that casts doubt on its capacity to meet the city's lot width requirements for a given\n zone - city staff will measure the lot width at the front yard setback to determine\n whether it meets this requirement by way of the following process:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n \n \n \n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Flag lots require a minimum thirty-foot of street frontage.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The front yard setback may be reduced to fifteen (15) feet for the residential living\n area or side entry designed garage; however, a street facing garage entrance shall\n be located a minimum twenty (20) feet beyond the sidewalk or sidewalk easement.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n 4.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Certain structures and projections are permitted within the required yard setback\n area, unless their placement there would interfere with building code provisions.\n Items permitted there include: Cornices, canopies, eaves or other like projections,\n which do not increase the volume of space enclosed by the building as determined by\n the Director, in consultation with the building official. None of these items shall\n project into a designated side yard more than two (2) feet or extend to within three\n (3) feet of a property line. It should be noted, that even though certain structures\n or projections are permitted within the yard setback, they are likely not permitted\n within an easement or right-of-way.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n 5.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Exterior steps or stairs shall not project into the designated side yard setback.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n 6.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Setbacks are typically measured from the property line; however, if a public sidewalk\n is placed upon private property by way of a public easement - the private property\n side edge of the sidewalk shall serve as the beginning of the setback line for establishing\n the yard setback.\n

\n \t\t\n \n

\n C.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n For all residential and/or commercial/industrial districts:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 1.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The term \"maximum lot coverage\" assumes all of the required onsite development functions\n necessary to support the development as a feature of lot coverage requirements are\n satisfied. These functions include: On-site parking; landscaping; building separation\n distances; travel aisle widths; solid waste collection device placement; easements;\n sidewalks; walkways; internal streets; irrigation, water and waste water systems;\n lawns; lighting; drainage facilities; parks; open spaces; public dedications; service\n areas and other land use support functions requiring physical space.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 2.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n The Director has administrative authority to modify side or rear setback requirements\n and height restrictions by up to twenty (20) percent with the Commission's concurrence,\n provided building or fire code separation distances and other development requirements\n are not compromised by that action.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 3.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n When a commercial and/or industrial use abuts a residential zoning district, the yard\n setback requirements shall be the same as required in the adjacent residential district.\n When residents are located in commercial or industrial zones, the yard setbacks are\n the same as required for the R-4 residential zoning district.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 4.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Odd lot size or topographical dimensional issues: The director will determine how\n to address area and setback requirements for odd shaped lots and land with topographical\n issues.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n 5.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Land use violation: The city shall not accept land use plans or time extension requests,\n if prior to their submission, the city has advised the property owner, or their representative,\n of an illegal or improper land use action or activity on the subject parcel, and in\n the interim, it has not been addressed to the city's satisfaction.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (Ord. No. 2024-06, § 2, 4-16-2024)\n
